statement: An order-three element of the full punctured-torus loop-outer group fixes no nonzero Fhat2-to-Cq character for any prime q different from three. Thus A_q minus the identity is invertible over Zq for q different from three and injective at every prime. Every full fixed group of an actual order-three representative lies in F prime. A2 is faithful on every finite torus subgroup, excluding C12 and D24 from D52. At any nontrivial cubic multiplier coordinate q, the only remaining matrix is the exact scalar lambda_q squared times the identity.
depends_on: D27 actual order-three lift; D48 labelled cusp-normalizer cube with unit three-adic exponent and primary cyclotomic homology; exact finite-index surface-cover completion and boundary homology; deck averaging at a prime-to-three covering degree; D33 finite order bound; D52 faithful-image classification
manuscript_passages: Section 30, folios 194-196, scans 383-387; Section 31, folios 198-199 verso, scans 391-394; Part D(b), full loop-outer finite actions in type (1,1)
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The invariant character is extended to the actual semidirect product. Its kernel is the specified type-(1,q) finite cover, and the cusp root lies in that exact extension by its cube equation. The homology splitting is the explicit deck-average idempotent and the index-q lattice inclusion, not a replacement of the full group by a pro-p quotient.
notes: The peripheral element v has v cubed equal to c to the kappa with kappa3 a unit. An invariant character to Cq places v in the cover extension and fixes each lifted boundary class. Averaging over the deck Cq splits the Z3 homology into the fixed boundary augmentation and the base torus cyclotomic module. The cubic norm is zero modulo three on both. Writing v=n s therefore makes its cube zero in mod-three cover homology, whereas the primitive lifted boundary c to kappa has nonzero class. This contradiction excludes invariant characters. The scalar nontrivial cubic multiplier branch remains explicitly unresolved, as does geometric conjugacy.
